question: does the batch-2D (TM, line source) slope model reproduce the true-3D (point dipole, 3D spreading) interface response on identical geometry, grid and materials — i.e. can t3 2D stand in for 3D in batch generation
design: same smooth interface line (t3: z=0.2y+22.625 clamped at outcrop) realised by one generator for both mothers; identical 5 cm grid, PML thickness 1.0 m, HORIPML + archived pml_cfs, dispersive Debye cover (dispersion_materials_v0.1), non-dispersive rock; only dimensionality differs

staircase.rule: zif_c = floor((0.2*ycen+22.625)/0.05 + 0.5), strips 0.25 m, clamp at surface = natural outcrop

comparisons.a_dimensionality: B3D5CM-C3mS2X-BG-T17 vs B2D5CM-C3mS2X-BG-CO33-t17 (same grid, same materials, same strips)
comparisons.b_grid: B2D5CM-C3mS2X-BG-CO33-t* vs archived batch2d_slope_t3_co B2D-C3mS2X-BG-CO33-t* (2.5 cm vs 5 cm, same line; staircase quantisation differs by design)

scaled_128M.note: linear in cells; Debye ADE adds one pole accumulator
